name: Hermes
overview: Hermes is a male figure mentioned briefly in the New Testament. He is noted for receiving greetings from the Apostle Paul, indicating his connection to the early Christian community. There is no information about his tribe or additional personal details in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Hermes appears as a proper name in the New Testament, specifically in Romans 16:14. No special meaning or divine origin is attributed to this name in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Hermes beyond the greeting he receives from Paul. No further relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Hermes is significant primarily because Paul sends greetings to him, showing that he was a recognized member of the early church community. This brief mention underscores the interconnectedness of believers and the importance of fellowship within the body of Christ. Though little is known about Hermes personally, his inclusion in Paul's greetings reflects his role as a faithful Christian in the Roman church.
